newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Cathay Life Insurance in telecom venture.
newsitem.headline: Cathay Life Insurance in telecom venture.

text.p: Cathay Life Insurance Company, Taiwan's largest insurance firm, said on Wednesday it would invest T$125 million in a telecommunications venture to provide mobile telephone service in northern Taiwan.
Cathay has signed a joint venture agreement with KG Telecom, owned by Taiwan's Koo's Group, Microelectronics Technology and U.S. firm Sprint.
KG Telecom, capitalised at T$2.5 billion, was one of the eight companies awarded the lucrative mobile phone franchises in January.

Under reform laws enacted in January 1996, foreign interests may own just 20 percent of Taiwan firms offering common-carrier services, a ratio designed by parliament to ensure local control of what is considered a strategic resource.
Common-carrier services are the main telephone and data lines in Taiwan's telecom network, including mobile telephony and retail telephone services.
Since January 1996, foreigners have been free to operate internet services, airline reservation systems and other value-added services that piggy-back common carrier networks.
